name: Muscadine Grape

facts.where: East Texas woods, climbing high into trees

caution: No toxic look-alikes when the fruit is present, but confirm the plant before eating any wild grape relative. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Muscadines hang high; the ripe ones drop, so check the ground under a loaded vine in September. Pop the sweet pulp from the tough skin with your teeth.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: The famous Southern grape: heavy, musky, and sweet. Cook the skins with the pulp for jelly the color of garnet.

photos.credit: Bob Peterson from North Palm Beach, Florida, Planet Earth!
